newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar softens, Central Bank intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar softens, Central Bank intervenes.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar softened to close at 472.50/473.50 per dollar after Central Bank intervention brought it back from 474 lows in a busy session, traders said.
The unit closed Monday at 472.00/473.00 per dollar.

"The market opened strong with businesses buying a lot of dollars in an illiquid market," said one broker. "That took the bolivar up to 474 per dollar at one point... then the Central Bank came in strong," he added.
Traders said dollar buying had increased as public debate over the bolivar's real value gained steam.
"Some say the bolivar should be revalued, others such as the IMF say that it should fall in line with inflation," said one trader.
"But either way, the Central Bank is coming and setting the rate at a level it thinks appropriate," he added.
